bibliography.note: Title 'Smallmouth Bass' (MDIFW, Fish & Wildlife → Fisheries → Species Information); undated (read 2026-11-26). The paper cites it in the text as '(MDIFW species page)', without 'n.d.', in §3.5.3 and §3.5.6, so show.mjs and the ledger did not link it: the ledger's sections for this key (§3.8.2–§3.8.6) are those of the generic 'MDIFW n.d.' label, not this page's. The in-text form should be '(MDIFW n.d., smallmouth bass page)'.

claims.quote: Bass grow slowly in Maine, but they can live for many years
claims.conditions: general statement; the page adds that a trophy bass of about 20 in 'could be around 20 years old'

claims.claim: MDIFW places Maine bass over rocky areas and drop-offs at 1.5–4.6 m
claims.quote: found in shallow rocky areas or off rocky drop offs in 5 to 15 feet
claims.conditions: 'In the spring and summer months'; angling advice, not a survey or telemetry result; 5–15 ft = 1.52–4.57 m
claims.note: The page limits it to spring and summer and gives it as a fishing tip; the rewrite could say 'in spring and summer, MDIFW's angling advice places bass…'.

notes: Both quotations are on the page. Other content: adults of 2–3 lb in most bass waters, few over 4 lb and rare over 5 lb in Maine, state record 8 lb; juveniles eat insects, adults fish, crayfish, frogs, newts and dragonflies; males guard eggs and young for weeks; introduced in the late 1800s, now throughout southern, central and eastern Maine; managed as a sport fishery in the southern half, with harvest of smaller bass encouraged. The code's smallmouth comments that cite 'MDIFW' (src/species.js:626–629 and :634, e.g. crayfish '60–90 %' of the adult diet, nests at 1–3 m once the water passes ~15 °C, guarding 25–35 days, feeding stops below ~10 °C, crayfish 'the adult's staple') do not come from this page, which gives none of those values; they must rest on another MDIFW document (probably Jordan 2001's assessment) and should name it.
